subsystems.name: Accelerator complex
subsystems.role: performs the matrix multiplications at the heart of transformer inference.

subsystems.name: Memory and interconnect
subsystems.role: holds model weights and moves data between accelerators fast enough to keep them fed.
parts: unified memory pool or discrete VRAM

subsystems.name: Host and control
subsystems.role: runs the operating system, schedules inference requests and manages storage.

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: stores model files, which can run to hundreds of gigabytes.

subsystems.name: Thermal and power
subsystems.role: removes heat from high-wattage accelerators and delivers stable power.
parts: heatsinks and fans or liquid cooling loop

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: runs the model efficiently on the hardware.
parts: inference engine such as llama.cpp or vLLM

buildSteps.title: Size the memory
buildSteps.detail: Decide which model sizes must fit: this sets the number of GPUs or the amount of unified memory needed.

buildSteps.title: Design power and cooling
buildSteps.detail: Add up the wattage of all accelerators and CPUs, then specify a power supply and a cooling loop or airflow path that can remove that heat.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Mount the CPU, system memory, accelerators and NVMe drives into a chassis or rack, seating cards and connecting power cables.

buildSteps.title: Wire the high-speed links
buildSteps.detail: Attach multiple accelerators with PCIe risers or NVLink bridges so they can share data directly rather than over the slow host bus.

buildSteps.title: Install the operating system
buildSteps.detail: Load a Linux distribution or macOS, then install GPU drivers and the matching compute toolkit.

buildSteps.title: Set up the inference runtime
buildSteps.detail: Install an inference engine, compile or download the appropriate kernels, and configure it to see all accelerators.

buildSteps.title: Quantise and load models
buildSteps.detail: Convert model weights to lower precision — commonly 4-bit or 8-bit — so they fit in memory and run at usable speed.

buildSteps.title: Benchmark and tune
buildSteps.detail: Measure tokens per second, adjust batch size and layer offloading between accelerators, and check temperatures under sustained load.

prerequisites.why: accelerators need to read billions of weights quickly; HBM and 2.5D packaging put memory next to the compute.
multiple accelerators must exchange activations and weights without stalling on a slow host bus.
techniques that avoid materialising the full attention matrix cut memory use and speed up inference.
reducing weights to 4-bit or 8-bit shrinks models enough to fit in affordable memory.

prerequisites.tech: Low-power AI accelerators for home use
prerequisites.why: most high-performance accelerators draw hundreds of watts and are costly, limiting home deployment.

pathway.milestone: single-GPU or unified-memory systems running 7B–70B parameter models locally
pathway.unlocks: private, offline chat and coding assistants on a desk.

pathway.milestone: multi-GPU home servers with 256 GB or more of unified memory running models with hundreds of billions of parameters
pathway.unlocks: near-cloud quality locally, with no data leaving the home.

pathway.milestone: dedicated low-power inference chips and standardised compute modules
local agentic AI orchestrating home devices and personal data
pathway.unlocks: privacy-preserving automation that works without a cloud connection.
